Momentary

/MOH-muhn-tair-ee/ - the stress falls on MOH · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Momentary means lasting only an instant.

A momentary hush fell over the courtroom as the foreman rose to speak, and then everyone spoke at once.

Worked Example

The photograph that made her name shows a heron, a leaping fish, and the rising sun stacked in one line — an alignment that was momentary in the strictest sense. She had anchored the boat at that bend for six straight sunrises; the seventh gave her the picture, and by the time the shutter reset, the fish was down and the line was broken forever.

Momentary is the exact word because it names what lasts only an instant — not merely short, but over almost as it begins. An intermission is short; a flash of alignment, a catch of breath, a shadow crossing a field is momentary. And note the trap waiting one letter away: momentous means important, a different word entirely.

How Momentary Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

brief

brief: short, but roomier — a brief meeting can run twenty minutes

flickering

flickering: appearing and disappearing in quick pulses

Antonyms

lasting

lasting: staying on after the moment has passed

drawn-out

drawn-out: stretched well beyond its natural length

How Strong Is It? — short → momentary → split-second

short vs. momentary

short vs. momentary: A short delay might still cost you ten minutes; momentary shrinks the claim to a single instant.

split-second vs. momentary

split-second vs. momentary: Split-second goes past momentary — over before you can even register that it began.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — moment

Root — moment: an instant; originally 'a movement' (Latin momentum)

Suffix — -ary

Suffix — -ary: relating to

Put it together

Put it together: Moment (an instant) + -ary (relating to) = lasting just a moment. Latin momentum began as 'a movement' — the tiny push that tips a scale — and shrank into 'the smallest slice of time a movement takes.' Momentary keeps that smallness: whatever it describes fits inside one tip of the scale.

Use the root in a new word: momentum

Use the root in a new word: momentum: The sled gathered momentum on the long hill and could not be stopped at the bottom.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Momentary is for what lasts a single instant. Its cluster-mates in this unit divide the longer stretches: ephemeral gives a thing a short but whole life — a day, one summer of fame — while transitory merely denies permanence, however slowly it goes. And do not mistake momentary for momentous, which means important.
